chapter: Making A Great Day in Harlem
title: Finding Mona Hinton's home movie
summary: Milt Hinton's home movie of the 1958 shoot spurred her to start, and David Berger's students found the film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Can you believe it? He’s America’s sweetheart. I mean his feet never touch the ground. He’s in this festival and that jazz party and they yank him back and forth overseas, he’s in Switzerland, he’s in Texas, he’s here he’s there. They never — well that was part of my problem, trying to get that footage. What made me decide to do the movie was him telling me about this home movie that she’d taken. So I just figured I’d better step on it because these people are dropping like flies. Lawrence Brown had just died that August, and Roy Eldridge had died the January before. So I thought I’d better get moving. So I started in without having seen the home movie. And then after a while I got quite a bit of stuff in the box and we got Sue on the case and she started doing her weaving and knitting and editing, and I still hadn’t seen the thing. And I got a little panicked and I enlisted a fellow called David Berger. Do you know him?

Yes he did the books. He’s the one that went down in that basement, which must be like Fibber McGee’s closet, and found a lot of wonderful photographs and got Milt to caption them so they knew who they were, and so I said to him, he teaches sociology in Philadelphia. I said, “get two of your Phi Beta students and go down there and look at every piece of celluloid you can find.” And they finally found the film.
How much actual footage was it? Time-wise?

It’s only 11 minutes. But Sue picked out little pieces. And a lot of it was damaged too, I mean she used as much as she could. But I said to Milt, “do you mean to say the photograph comes to life?” And he says, “yeah, you could say that.” And it does. Because as a static picture, it’s black and white. And then when it comes to life there’s color. And that’s a nice touch I think.
